result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers keep stale content dimmed, use a 300ms threshold with a minimum display time, and specify a clear failure banner with Retry, kept separate from the zero-results state. B scores higher on placement and layout stability: the map gets its own 'Updating pins…' pill, the progress line takes no layout space, the count and cards swap together, and skeletons are limited to the first load or a large area change. A is very precise on timing and handles a partial failure (list loads, pins fail), but on the map the only loading signal is dimmed pins, so the signal near the map is weaker. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers keep stale results visible, wait 300ms before showing anything, and handle failure well, with a plain-language banner, a Retry button and a warning mark on the changed chip. B is more thorough on layout stability: it reserves space for the banner, explains when skeletons fit and when they don't, and asks for a check that no empty frame appears. It also covers partial failure, a 'Still working…' state with Cancel, and exact timing specs. A localizes loading a little better with a dedicated map pill, while B deliberately keeps one indicator and only dims the pins.
